newsitem.title: UK: Southern Elect says power restored to 90 pct.
newsitem.headline: Southern Elect says power restored to 90 pct.

text.p: UK regional electricity distributor Southern Electric said it has restored supplies to over 90 percent of customers who were affected by the severe gales in the south of England on Monday night, bringing the number who are still without electricity down to around 4,000.
Some 50,000 customers were without electricity at the height of the storm but that number was reduced to 10,000 by 2330 GMT last night, said the company in a statement.
Engineers are continuing to repair overhead lines and equipment damaged by the 85 miles per hour winds.

"We expect that the majority of customers supplies should be restored by lunchtime and we will continue to work to ensure that everyone is back on supply by early evening," said Colin Hood, Southern's director of distribution.
The worst hit area of the country was the south where gusts of up to 90mph were reported from Cornwall to Kent.
Although weather forecasters had predicted the gale force storms to last through the night by 0300 GMT they seemed to have exhausted themselves.
Some cross-Channel passenger ferries were prevented from berthing at Dover, although the port remained open.
